basic_identification.full_title: General Construction in Steel — Code of Practice
basic_identification.sector_category: Civil Engineering (approved by the Civil Engineering Division Council of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

sectional_committee.name: Structural Engineering and Structural Sections Sectional Committee

scope.summary: This standard applies to general construction using hot rolled steel sections joined using riveting, bolting, and welding. It gives general guidance as regards the various loads, limits of strength, serviceability, durability, and fire resistance to be considered in design. Specific provisions for special structures such as bridges, chimneys, cranes, tanks, transmission line towers, bulk storage structures, tubular structures, and cold-formed light gauge steel sections are explicitly excluded as they are covered in separate standards.

certification_and_marking.disclaimer: No mandatory BIS product certification (such as the ISI Mark) is strictly required within the code of practice text itself for finished, erected structures. However, material-level marking and quality confirmation rules are explicitly defined as follows:

requirements.provision: All structural steel used in general construction must conform to IS 2062 before fabrication begins.
Structural steel that is not backed by mill test certificates is restricted only to unimportant members. Alternatively, its quality must be verified by executing tensile tests according to IS 1608.
A marking diagram allotting distinct identification marks to each separate part of the steelwork must be prepared to facilitate site assembly and erection.
Welders executing structural work must present satisfactory evidence of completing qualifying tests per IS 817, IS 1393, IS 7307 (Part 1), IS 7310 (Part 1), or IS 7318 (Part 1).
The manufacturer must guarantee compliance with the provisions of IS 800 if required to do so by the purchaser.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 800:2007 is the foundational Indian Standard code of practice governing the design, fabrication, and erection of structural steelwork, primarily utilizing hot-rolled steel sections. It should be cited and followed for any general steel structures, building frames, or industrial sheds constructed in India. The standard prioritises the modern Limit State Design (LSD) method while keeping Working Stress Design (WSD) as an acceptable alternative. A critical technical detail to double-check when using this standard is the width-to-thickness ratio classification of cross-section elements (Class 1 to 4). This classification determines if the structure will fail prematurely due to local buckling before reaching full plastic yield capacity. Additionally, all structural steel must be verified to conform with IS 2062.
